title: Upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For each integer $d\geq0$, the set $$\{s\in S\mid\dim X_s\leq d\}$$ is open, where $X_s$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Fix an integer $d\geq0$. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and finite type includes locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each $x\in X$ write $\widetilde x$ for its corresponding point in $X_{f(x)}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open] with $n=d$: $U_d=\{x:\dim_{\widetilde x}X_{f(x)}\leq d\}$ is open. Thus its complement $Z_d=\{x:\dim_{\widetilde x}X_{f(x)}>d\}$ is closed in $X$.

By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $f$ is universally closed. Apply the defining condition to the identity base change $S\to S$, whose pullback is $f$ itself. Hence the underlying map $f:|X|\to|S|$ takes closed subsets to closed subsets, and $C_d=f(Z_d)$ is closed in $S$.

For $s\in S$, the fibre projection identifies the points of $X_s$ with $f^{-1}(s)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] to the topological space $|X_s|$: $\dim X_s=\sup_{z\in X_s}\dim_zX_s$. If $s\in C_d$, choose $x\in Z_d$ with $f(x)=s$; its corresponding $z\in X_s$ has $\dim_zX_s>d$, so the supremum is greater than $d$. Conversely, if $s\notin C_d$, every $x\in f^{-1}(s)$ lies outside $Z_d$, so every $z\in X_s$ has $\dim_zX_s\leq d$; their supremum is at most $d$. Therefore $s\in C_d$ if and only if $\dim X_s>d$. If the fibre is empty, the supremum is $-\infty\leq d$ and there is no point mapping to $s$, so the same equivalence holds.

The previous equivalence gives $\{s\in S:\dim X_s\leq d\}=S\setminus C_d$. This is open because $C_d$ is closed. The construction works for every $d\geq0$, and uses neither Noetherianity nor flatness.
